transcript.text: Hi, I'm Sensei. Put your page under the camera and start solving. I'm watching.
You multiplied speed by time, but the units don't match—what unit is the speed in, and what unit should it be to get distance in meters?
The speed's in km per hour. Should it be meters per second? So like divide by 3.6?
Yes, you're right—speed must be in meters per second to get distance in meters. To convert km/h to m/s, divide by 3.6. Try that with 72 km/h and see what you get.
72 over 3.6 is 20 meters per second, so 20 times 5 is 100 meters. Why is it 3.6 though?
The number 3.6 comes from how many meters are in a kilometer and how many seconds are in an hour. Try converting 10 km/h to m/s to see the pattern.
Um, 10 km is 10000 meters, and an hour is 3600 seconds, so 10000 over 3600? That's like 2.8?
To convert km/h to m/s, you divide by 3.6 because 1 km is 1000 meters and 1 hour is 3600 seconds. Try converting 20 km/h to m/s using that idea.
Oh wait, 3600 divided by 1000 is 3.6. So that's why. So my answer is 20 meters per second times 5, 100 meters. Thanks.
